The implementation of chatrooms is a nice addition, but I think it can be expanded upon.

Due to the chatroom's lack of message storage, users will lose all of their history every time they click on a link or refresh the page. This can be ameliorated by giving the chat box its own dedicated web page, so that users can keep the chat running in one tab while browsing the rest of Voat in another. Having a whole page will also be more convenient than having a tiny box in the sidebar since there's more space for reading long messages and scrolling through history.

Adding IRC access would also be useful. IRC is ubiquitous among many communities, and integrating it into Voat's chat system would be very convenient for users who already have their preferred client installed on their desktop, tablet, and/or phone especially since many clients can save logs unlike the web frontend.

The IRC login process could be done as such:

  1. Connect to irc.voat.co
  2. Give the server your Voat username and password credentials
  3. Join subverse channel created by the server
Expand on the subverse chatroom functionality by giving it a dedicated web frontend and IRC access
Another thing that could be done, instead of having a separate page is having the chat in a dedicated box like scrollback.

I think IRC could be nice but I think it there should only be a handful of channels and not one for every subverse (unless every subverse wants one).

I'd much rather have a general chat, admin/moderator chat (for users to discuss the site with the "higher ups"), and a few niche channels, technology, lifestyle, etc. My reasoning is, the community is still relatively small and I'd like to see fewer, more active channels/subverses, then a ton of inactive channels/subverses.
